title: Agents and Agentic Systems
lede: An agent is an LLM running in a control loop: it observes the world, decides what to do, calls tools, observes the results, and repeats until the goal is reached. This chapter covers the four canonical agent loops, single- vs multi-agent orchestration, state machines and workflow graphs, agent memory, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, subagents, error recovery, durable long-running execution, and browser / computer-use agents.

bn.title: Agent আর Agentic System
bn.lede: Agent হলো একটা LLM, যা একটা control loop-এর ভেতরে চলে। সে চারপাশ দেখে (observe), কী করবে ঠিক করে, tool call করে, ফলাফল দেখে, আর লক্ষ্যে না পৌঁছানো পর্যন্ত এটা বারবার করে। এই অধ্যায়ে আছে: চারটা প্রচলিত agent loop, single-agent বনাম multi-agent orchestration, state machine আর workflow graph, agent memory, human-in-the-loop checkpoint, subagent, error recovery, দীর্ঘ সময় ধরে চলা durable execution, আর browser / computer-use agent।

sections.title: What an agent actually is
sections.sub: A working definition, the boundary between "agent" and "workflow," and the minimum set of components any production agent must have.

bn.title: Agent আসলে কী
bn.sub: একটা কাজ চালানোর মতো সংজ্ঞা, "agent" আর "workflow"-এর মধ্যে সীমারেখা, আর যেকোনো production agent-এ অন্তত কী কী component থাকতেই হবে।

body.html: Strip away the marketing and every agent is the same shape: a loop that takes the current state, asks an LLM what to do next, executes the answer (a tool call, a structured response, or a final answer), and feeds the result back in. Where agents diverge from each other is how the loop is structured, what the state contains, and how failure is handled.

# The minimal agent in 12 lines
def agent_loop(goal, llm, tools, max_steps=20):
    history = [{"role": "user", "content": goal}]
    for step in range(max_steps):
        response = llm.complete(history, tools=tools)
        if response.finish_reason == "stop":
            return response.text
        result = tools.invoke(response.tool_call)
        history.append({"role": "tool", "content": str(result)})
    raise AgentTimeout("loop did not terminate")

A workflow is a deterministic graph of LLM calls and tool calls: every step is authored, every branch is explicit. An agent is a workflow where at least one node's behaviour is decided at runtime by the LLM itself. The line is blurry in practice — most production systems are "agentic workflows" that combine both.

blocks.html: Rule of thumb: if a human could write a flowchart of the system's behaviour from the prompt alone, it's a workflow. If the LLM picks the next node at runtime, it's an agent. Most shipped systems are a mix — deterministic scaffolding around a few agentic decisions.

items: A bounded loop with a hard step cap and a wall-clock timeout. Unbounded loops are how agents burn $10k overnight.
A tool surface that's narrow, well-typed, and namespaced (so the model can't accidentally call a destructive tool without going through a guardrail).
A scratchpad — some persistent state across turns that survives the LLM's context window. Either the model writes to a file, the framework keeps it, or you stuff it into the next prompt.
An exit predicate: at minimum, "I think I have enough; here is the answer." Without one the agent will keep acting forever.
Observability: every step recorded with prompt, tool call, result, cost, and latency. Without it you cannot debug.

layman.html: An agent is an AI that doesn't stop until the job is done. A normal chatbot: you ask, it answers, done. An agent: you ask "find me a hotel under $150 in Tokyo next week," and it goes off, browses the web, checks three sites, compares them, and comes back in five minutes with a recommendation. You didn't tell it which sites. It figured that out.
The "loop" is just doing the same five steps over and over:

1. Look at what's in front of me (what tools do I have? what have I learned so far?).
2. Decide what to do next (use a tool, ask the user, or stop).
3. Do it (call the tool, send the message).
4. Look at the result.
5. Repeat from step 1 until done (or until you've been looping too long).

The five things every production agent must have: a cap on how many times it can loop, a small list of allowed tools, a place to keep notes that survive the model's short memory, a way to say "I'm done," and a way to record what it did so you can debug it later. Skip any one and you have a hobby project, not a product.

blocks.html: The personal-assistant analogy: an agent is like hiring a human PA. The PA doesn't know your preferences yet (it builds them over time). When you ask "handle my dentist appointment," the PA calls the dentist, asks for times, checks your calendar, calls back to confirm, and texts you the details. If the dentist's line is busy, the PA tries again in 5 minutes. If you said "cancel if it costs more than $200," the PA pauses and asks before booking. If the PA's phone dies, it picks up where it left off when it charges. That's an agent.

bangla.html: Agent হলো একটি LLM যা একটি control loop-এ চলে — পরিবেশ দেখে, সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়, টুল কল করে, ফলাফল দেখে এবং লক্ষ্য পূরণ না হওয়া পর্যন্ত পুনরাবৃত্তি করে।
ন্যূনতম agent: একটি লুপ যা বর্তমান state নেয়, LLM-কে জিজ্ঞেস করে "পরে কী করবে," উত্তর execute করে এবং ফলাফল ফিরিয়ে দেয়।
Agent বনাম workflow: workflow হলো LLM কল ও টুল কলের একটি নির্ধারিত গ্রাফ। Agent হলো এমন একটি workflow যেখানে কমপক্ষে একটি node-এর আচরণ runtime-এ LLM নিজেই সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়।
প্রতিটি প্রোডাকশন agent-এর যা থাকা দরকার: একটি সীমিত লুপ, একটি সংকীর্ণ ও টাইপ করা টুল surface, একটি scratchpad, একটি exit predicate, এবং observability।

blocks.html: ব্যক্তিগত সহকারীর উপমা: এজেন্ট হলো একজন PA নিয়োগ করার মতো। PA আপনার পছন্দ জানে না (সময়ের সাথে শেখে)। "ডেন্টিস্টের অ্যাপয়েন্টমেন্ট ঠিক কর" বললে সে ফোন করে, সময় জিজ্ঞেস করে, ক্যালেন্ডার দেখে, নিশ্চিত করে আপনাকে জানায়।

en.title: Watch an agent loop until it finishes
en.why: When you build an AI that checks prices or books tickets, it must work step by step and know when to stop. If it never stops, it keeps calling tools and you pay for every call.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt:
You are an agent that works in a loop. You can use two tools:
- get_price(item): returns the price of one item in BDT
- calculator(expression): returns the result of a math expression

Rules:
1. Each turn, reply with exactly ONE line. Either:
   ACTION: tool_name(argument)
   or
   FINAL: your answer
2. After an ACTION line, stop and wait. I will reply with a line that starts with OBSERVATION.
3. You have at most 6 steps. If you reach step 6 without an answer, write FINAL: step limit reached.

Goal: Find the total cost of 3 notebooks and 4 pens.
steps.expect: One line only, for example ACTION: get_price(notebook). Then the model waits for you.
steps.example: ACTION: get_price(notebook)

steps.do: Now you are the tool. Copy this price list, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: OBSERVATION: notebook = 120 BDT, pen = 25 BDT
steps.expect: A new ACTION line. Most chats ask for the calculator, for example ACTION: calculator(3 * 120 + 4 * 25). If the model asks for a price again, send the same price list again.
steps.example: ACTION: calculator(3 * 120 + 4 * 25)

steps.do: Work out the sum on a phone calculator. Type OBSERVATION: and the number, then press Enter. For 3 * 120 + 4 * 25 the answer is 460.
steps.expect: One line that starts with FINAL, for example FINAL: The total cost is 460 BDT.
steps.example: FINAL: The total cost of 3 notebooks and 4 pens is 460 BDT.

steps.do: Copy this question, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Which of your lines told the loop to stop? Who chose that moment: you or me?
steps.expect: The model points to its FINAL line and says it chose to stop by itself.
steps.example: The FINAL line told the loop to stop. I chose that moment myself, because I had the total and needed no more tools.

en.learned: You never told the model which tool to call first. It chose each action, read your result, and chose the next one. It stopped when it wrote FINAL, so the model decided when the work was done. The rule at most 6 steps is a step limit: it stops a loop that never ends.
en.done: You have seen 2 or 3 ACTION lines and then one FINAL line with the total 460 BDT.

check.question: What makes this an agent and not a fixed list of steps?
check.answer: The model decides the next step and decides when to stop. In a fixed list of steps, a person writes every step in advance.

en.challenge: Change the rule to at most 2 steps and use the same goal in a new chat. What does the agent write when 2 steps are too few?

bn.title: দেখো, agent কীভাবে loop চালিয়ে শেষ করে
bn.why: তুমি যখন এমন AI বানাবে যা দাম দেখে বা ticket book করে, তখন সে ধাপে ধাপে কাজ করবে এবং কখন থামতে হবে তা জানবে। সে যদি কখনও না থামে, তাহলে সে বারবার tool call করতেই থাকবে, আর প্রতিটা call-এর জন্য তোমাকে টাকা দিতে হবে।

steps.do: এই prompt টা copy করো, chat-এ paste করে Enter চাপো।
steps.prompt:
তুমি একটা agent, যে loop-এ কাজ করে। তোমার দুটো tool আছে:
- get_price(item): একটা জিনিসের দাম BDT-তে দেয়
- calculator(expression): একটা অঙ্কের ফল দেয়

নিয়ম:
1. প্রতি turn-এ ঠিক ১টা লাইন লেখো। হয়:
   ACTION: tool_name(argument)
   অথবা
   FINAL: তোমার উত্তর
2. ACTION লাইনের পর থেমে অপেক্ষা করো। আমি OBSERVATION দিয়ে শুরু হওয়া একটা লাইন পাঠাব।
3. তোমার সর্বোচ্চ ৬টা step আছে। ৬ নম্বর step-এ পৌঁছেও উত্তর না পেলে লেখো: FINAL: step limit reached.

লক্ষ্য: ৩টা notebook আর ৪টা pen-এর মোট দাম বের করো।
steps.expect: শুধু একটা লাইন, যেমন ACTION: get_price(notebook)। তারপর model তোমার জন্য অপেক্ষা করে।
steps.example: ACTION: get_price(notebook)

steps.do: এবার তুমি tool। এই দামের তালিকা copy করে paste করো, তারপর Enter চাপো। (এটা English-এ রাখা হয়েছে, কারণ tool-এর উত্তর সাধারণত English-এ হয়।)
steps.prompt: OBSERVATION: notebook = 120 BDT, pen = 25 BDT
steps.expect: নতুন একটা ACTION লাইন। বেশির ভাগ chat calculator চায়, যেমন ACTION: calculator(3 * 120 + 4 * 25)। model আবার দাম চাইলে একই তালিকা আবার পাঠাও।
steps.example: ACTION: calculator(3 * 120 + 4 * 25)

steps.do: phone-এর calculator-এ যোগফলটা বের করো। OBSERVATION: লিখে সংখ্যাটা লেখো, তারপর Enter চাপো। 3 * 120 + 4 * 25-এর উত্তর 460।
steps.expect: FINAL দিয়ে শুরু হওয়া একটা লাইন, যেমন FINAL: মোট দাম 460 BDT।
steps.example: FINAL: ৩টা notebook আর ৪টা pen-এর মোট দাম 460 BDT।

steps.do: এই প্রশ্নটা copy করে paste করো, তারপর Enter চাপো।
steps.prompt: তোমার কোন লাইনটা loop-কে থামতে বলেছে? থামার সিদ্ধান্তটা কে নিয়েছে: তুমি, নাকি আমি?
steps.expect: model তার FINAL লাইন দেখায় এবং বলে যে থামার সিদ্ধান্ত সে নিজেই নিয়েছে।
steps.example: FINAL লাইনটাই loop-কে থামতে বলেছে। থামার সিদ্ধান্ত আমি নিজেই নিয়েছি, কারণ আমার কাছে মোট দাম ছিল আর আর কোনো tool লাগত না।

bn.learned: তুমি model-কে বলোনি কোন tool আগে call করতে হবে। সে নিজেই প্রতিটা action বেছেছে, তোমার result পড়েছে, তারপর পরের action বেছেছে। সে FINAL লিখে থেমেছে, মানে কাজ শেষ কি না তা model-ই ঠিক করেছে। সর্বোচ্চ ৬টা step নিয়মটার নাম step limit: এটা এমন loop থামায় যা কখনও শেষ হয় না।
bn.done: তুমি ২-৩টা ACTION লাইন আর তারপর মোট দাম 460 BDT-সহ একটা FINAL লাইন দেখেছ।

check.answer: model নিজেই ঠিক করে পরের ধাপ কী এবং কখন থামতে হবে। ধাপের তালিকায় একজন মানুষ আগে থেকেই প্রতিটা ধাপ লিখে রাখে।

sections.title: The four canonical agent loops
sections.sub: Every agent loop you'll meet in production is a variation of one of these four patterns. Pick by the shape of your task, not by hype.

body.html: Introduced by Yao et al. in 2022,[1] ReAct is the simplest agent loop: the model writes a Thought, picks an Action, observes the result, repeats. The thought is in the model's private scratchpad and never shown to the user; only the final answer is. ReAct is the default loop in LangChain's AgentExecutor and most early agent frameworks.

body.code:
# ReAct scratchpad format (text version)
Thought: I need to find the population of Tokyo in 2024.
Action:   search(query="Tokyo population 2024 official")
Observation: As of January 2024, the estimated population...
Thought: Now I can answer.
Action:   Finish("Tokyo's population is ~13.96 million.")
body.html:
# ReAct scratchpad format (text version)
Thought: I need to find the population of Tokyo in 2024.
Action:   search(query="Tokyo population 2024 official")
Observation: As of January 2024, the estimated population...

blocks.html: Why ReAct dominates: the interleaved reasoning makes traces human-readable. When something goes wrong, you can read the scratchpad and see why the model picked the action it did. That single property is why ReAct is still the default for most agent debugging.

body.html: Plan-and-Execute separates planning from execution: a planner (usually a strong LLM) produces a sequence of steps, then a worker (often a smaller model or a deterministic tool) carries out each step. The worker can be ReAct itself, a single-shot LLM call, or a pure function. If a step fails, the planner re-runs only that step (cheap) rather than the whole loop.[2]

Reflexion adds a second pass: after a ReAct attempt, the model is asked to reflect on what went wrong, and that reflection is appended to the memory for the next attempt.[3] In benchmarks (HumanEval, AlfWorld) Reflexion beats vanilla ReAct by 10–20% absolute.

ReWOO's insight: in many retrieval-heavy tasks, the model doesn't need to see the result of tool #1 to plan tool #2. It plans the entire tool graph upfront, the worker executes everything in parallel, then the solver reads the evidence and answers.[4] ReWOO uses 4–6× fewer tokens than ReAct on retrieval benchmarks.

rows: Default for short, tool-heavy tasks; debugging
Known-shape workflows; mixed executors per step

layman.html: There are four common "personalities" for agents:

• ReAct = the improv actor. Thinks out loud, acts, reacts.
• Plan-and-Execute = the project manager. Writes a to-do list, then ticks items off.
• Reflexion = the perfectionist. Does the work, checks itself, tries again.
• ReWOO = the efficient assistant. Plans every call upfront, no chat.

How to pick: default to ReAct. If your task is "go look up 5 things in parallel and write a summary," switch to ReWOO. If your task is "do these 6 steps in order, but be ready to replan if step 3 fails," use Plan-and-Execute.

blocks.html: The four-college analogy: ReAct is the liberal-arts student. Plan-and-Execute is the engineering student. Reflexion is the grad student. ReWOO is the consultant who preps the entire deck before the meeting.

bangla.html: চারটি ক্যানোনিক্যাল লুপ: ReAct, Plan-and-Execute, Reflexion, ReWOO।
কোনটা বেছে নেবেন: ReAct দিয়ে শুরু করুন। parallel-এ 5টি জিনিস খুঁজে summary লিখতে হলে ReWOO। 6-ধাপের sequence-এ ধাপ 3 ব্যর্থ হলে replan করতে হলে Plan-and-Execute।

blocks.html: চার-শিক্ষার্থীর উপমা: ReAct হলো liberal-arts শিক্ষার্থী। Plan-and-Execute হলো engineering শিক্ষার্থী। Reflexion হলো graduate শিক্ষার্থী। ReWOO হলো consultant।

en.title: Compare step-by-step and plan-first agents
en.why: When your agent must look up many facts, the way it plans changes how many AI calls you pay for. You can think after every result, or you can make one plan at the start.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Count the searches in the reply.
steps.prompt:
You are a planner. You have one tool: search(query), which returns a fact from a database.
Task: Find the population of Dhaka, Chattogram, and Sylhet, then give the total.

Plan ALL tool calls now, before you see any result. Use this format:
#E1 = search("...")
#E2 = search("...")
#E3 = search("...")
Solve: a short note on how you will combine #E1, #E2 and #E3.

Do not guess any number. Stop after the plan.
steps.expect: A plan with 3 searches written at once, and a short Solve note. No population numbers yet.
steps.example:
#E1 = search("population of Dhaka")
#E2 = search("population of Chattogram")
#E3 = search("population of Sylhet")
Solve: Add the three results #E1, #E2 and #E3 to get the total population.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Count the searches in the reply.
steps.prompt:
You are an agent that uses the ReAct format. You have one tool: search(query), which returns a fact from a database.
Task: Find the population of Dhaka, Chattogram, and Sylhet, then give the total.

Work in this format:
Thought: your reasoning
Action: search("...") or Finish("...")

Write only ONE Thought and ONE Action. Then stop and wait for my Observation. Do not guess any number.
steps.expect: Only 1 Thought and 1 Action, for example a search for Dhaka. Then the model waits.
steps.example:
Thought: I need the population of three cities. I will start with Dhaka.
Action: search("population of Dhaka")

steps.do: Now you are the search tool. Copy this result, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Observation: Dhaka has 10.2 million people.
steps.expect: A new Thought and one new Action, for example a search for Chattogram. The model still has 2 cities to go.
steps.example:
Thought: Dhaka has 10.2 million. I still need Chattogram and Sylhet. I will search Chattogram next.
Action: search("population of Chattogram")

en.learned: The plan-first agent wrote all 3 searches at once, because no search needs the result of another. The step-by-step agent (called ReAct) stops after each action, so it needs a new model call for each result. For these 3 cities, ReAct needs about 4 model calls and plan-first needs about 2. The price of plan-first is that you get no Thought lines, so it is harder to see why the model did something.
en.done: You have a plan with 3 searches from chat 1, and one Thought with one search from chat 2.

check.question: Why can the plan-first agent write all 3 searches at once?
check.answer: The 3 searches do not need each other's results. So the model can plan them all before it sees any result, and it needs fewer model calls.

en.challenge: Use this task in both prompts: Check if it rains in Dhaka today. If it rains, find an indoor museum. If not, find a park. Why is it hard to plan before you see the first result?

sections.title: Single-agent vs multi-agent orchestration
sections.sub: The most expensive mistake in agent engineering is reaching for a multi-agent setup when a well-tuned single agent would do.

bn.title: Single-agent বনাম multi-agent orchestration
bn.sub: Agent engineering-এর সবচেয়ে দামি ভুল হলো: ভালোভাবে tune করা একটা agent-ই যথেষ্ট ছিল, অথচ multi-agent setup বেছে নেওয়া।

body.html: What a single agent gives you
A single agent is one LLM in one control loop with one tool surface. Every decision flows through one prompt, one model call, one trace. Debugging is "read the trace."
What a multi-agent setup gives you
Multi-agent systems have an orchestrator that delegates to specialised workers — researcher, writer, critic, coder — each with its own prompt, its own tool surface, and (often) its own model.[5]

rows: One agent's failure can be retried independently

blocks.html: Anti-pattern: spinning up a multi-agent system because it sounds advanced. Anthropic's own engineering blog reports that well-tuned single-agent prompts often match multi-agent quality at a fraction of the cost.[5]

items: Shared scratchpad (blackboard): all agents read/write to a shared file or in-memory dict.
Message passing: orchestrator sends typed messages to workers.
Tool calls: the orchestrator is the only "agent"; workers are exposed as tools.

body.code:
# Anthropic Research pattern (simplified)
async def research(query):
    sub_queries = await orchestrator.plan(query)
    findings = await asyncio.gather(*[
        researcher.search(sq) for sq in sub_queries
    ])
    review = await critic.review(query, findings)
    return await orchestrator.synthesise(query, findings, review)
body.html:
# Anthropic Research pattern (simplified)
async def research(query):
    sub_queries = await orchestrator.plan(query)
    findings = await asyncio.gather(*[
        researcher.search(sq) for sq in sub_queries
    ])
    review = await critic.review(query, findings)
    return await orchestrator.synthesise(query, findings, review)

layman.html: "One smart assistant" vs "a team of specialists."
Why teams cost more: every time the manager hands work to a specialist, you have to send them the full context. The specialist has to re-read it. That's the 2–5× cost.
When to use a team: when one person really cannot do it all well.
The mistake to avoid: building a team because teams sound smart, when one well-tuned generalist would do.

blocks.html: The restaurant analogy: single-agent is a one-person food truck. Multi-agent is a restaurant with multiple specialists.

bangla.html: Single-agent বনাম Multi-agent: Single-agent সিস্টেমে একটি LLM একটি control loop-এ চলে। Multi-agent সিস্টেমে একজন orchestrator বিশেষায়িত workers-এ কাজ ভাগ করে দেয়।[5]
Anti-pattern: multi-agent সিস্টেম চালু করা কারণ এটি advanced শোনায়।

blocks.html: রেস্তোরাঁর উপমা: single-agent হলো one-person food truck। Multi-agent হলো বিশেষজ্ঞদের সাথে একটি রেস্তোরাঁ।

en.title: Compare one agent with a team of three
en.why: Many teams build a team of AI agents because it sounds powerful. A team costs more, so you must check that it really gives a better result than one good prompt.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Read the announcement and the note after it.
steps.prompt:
Write a 60-word announcement for a new app called TaskNest.
Notes from the team:
- Launch date: 12 March (from the marketing plan)
- Launch date: 15 March (from the engineering email)
- Price: 400 BDT per month
- Free trial: 14 days
- Main feature: shared to-do lists for small teams
If the notes have a conflict, say so after the announcement.
steps.expect: A short announcement (about 60 words) and a note about the two launch dates, 12 March and 15 March.
steps.example:
Meet TaskNest! Plan and share to-do lists with your small team in one simple app. No more lost notes or missed deadlines. Everyone sees the same list, updates tasks in real time, and knows who does what. Try it free for 14 days, then pay just 400 BDT per month. TaskNest launches soon, so get ready to organise your work together.
Note: The notes give two launch dates, 12 March (marketing plan) and 15 March (engineering email). Please confirm the date before you publish.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Now one AI acts as a team of three, with a leader.
steps.prompt:
Act as a team of three agents: Researcher, Writer, and Critic, with an Orchestrator who joins their work at the end. Show each agent's output under its own heading.
1. Researcher: list the facts and conflicts in the notes.
2. Writer: write a 60-word announcement for a new app called TaskNest.
3. Critic: review the draft against the facts and list problems.
4. Orchestrator: write the final announcement and say what changed.

Notes from the team:
- Launch date: 12 March (from the marketing plan)
- Launch date: 15 March (from the engineering email)
- Price: 400 BDT per month
- Free trial: 14 days
- Main feature: shared to-do lists for small teams
steps.expect: A much longer reply with 4 headings: Researcher, Writer, Critic, Orchestrator. The Researcher usually lists the date conflict.
steps.example:
Researcher: Facts: 400 BDT per month, 14-day free trial, shared to-do lists for small teams. Conflict: launch date is 12 March (marketing) or 15 March (engineering).
Writer: Meet TaskNest! Shared to-do lists for small teams. Try it free for 14 days, then 400 BDT per month. Launching 12 March.
Critic: The draft uses 12 March, but the date is not confirmed. It must not state one date as fact.
Orchestrator: Final: Meet TaskNest! … Launching soon. Changed: I removed the unconfirmed date and asked the team to confirm it.

steps.do: Look at both replies. Write down which reply is longer, and whether each reply found the date conflict.
steps.expect: The team reply is usually several times longer. Often both replies find the conflict between 12 March and 15 March.

en.learned: The team reply used many more words for the same job. More words mean more tokens (the pieces of text you pay for), so a team often costs 2 to 5 times more. The single prompt found the same date problem. A team is worth it only when the roles are really different or a mistake is costly.
en.done: You have two replies, and you know which one is longer and whether each one found the date conflict.

check.question: When is a team of agents worth the extra cost?
check.answer: When the roles are really different and a mistake is costly. For a small task about one topic, one good agent is cheaper and easier to debug.

sections.title: State machines and workflow graphs
sections.sub: For non-trivial agents, replace the implicit loop with an explicit graph of nodes (LLM calls, tool calls, human approvals) connected by edges (conditional transitions). This is how production systems stay debuggable.

bn.title: State machine আর workflow graph
bn.sub: সহজ নয় এমন agent-এর ক্ষেত্রে অদৃশ্য loop-এর জায়গায় একটা পরিষ্কার graph বানান। এর node হবে LLM call, tool call বা human approval, আর edge হবে শর্ত অনুযায়ী এক ধাপ থেকে আরেক ধাপে যাওয়া। এভাবেই production system-এ debug করা সহজ থাকে।

body.html: An implicit loop is fast to write and impossible to debug. After 30 tool calls, you can't tell which path the model took. An explicit graph makes the topology visible: every node has a name, every edge has a condition, every transition is recorded.

LangGraph (LangChain's graph framework) is the most popular Python/TypeScript option.[6] It models the agent as a state graph: nodes are functions, edges are conditional, the state is a TypedDict that flows through. Cycles are first-class (an agent can loop back to an earlier node), and checkpointer lets you resume from any past state.

body.code:
# LangGraph minimal agent
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from typing import TypedDict

class State(TypedDict):
    messages: list
    step: int

def call_llm(state: State) -> State:
    response = llm.invoke(state["messages"])
    return {"messages": state["messages"] + [response], "step": state["step"] + 1}

def should_continue(state: State) -> str:
    last = state["messages"][-1]
    if hasattr(last, "tool_calls") and last.tool_calls:
        return "tool"
    return END

graph = StateGraph(State)
graph.add_node("llm", call_llm)
graph.add_conditional_edges("llm", should_continue, {"tool": "llm", END: END})
graph.set_entry_point("llm")
app = graph.compile()

For long-running agents (minutes to hours), the graph needs to be durable — survive crashes, retries, and human-in-the-loop pauses. Temporal and Restate are workflow engines from the microservices world adapted to agents.[7] Mastra is TypeScript-first with built-in workflow engine, memory, and tool definitions. Inngest is event-driven serverless workflows with pay-per-step pricing.

layman.html: Don't write agents as a single loop; draw a map of the steps.

When an agent does "search → summarise → check → maybe search again → write answer," you could write that as one loop with if-statements. Or you could draw a flowchart with named boxes and arrows. The flowchart version is what graph frameworks do for you.
For long agents (hours/days): you need a workflow engine that survives crashes. That's Temporal or Restate.

Picking one: if you're already in Python + LangChain, use LangGraph. If you need long-running + humans in the loop, use Temporal. If you want everything in TypeScript with batteries included, try Mastra. If you wake on webhooks and want to pay per step, use Inngest.

blocks.html: The flowchart vs paragraph analogy: writing an agent as a loop is like writing directions as a paragraph. Drawing it as a graph is like giving someone a map.

en.title: Run a support ticket through a graph
en.why: When an agent can refund money, you must be able to prove which path it took. A graph with named steps gives you a log that you can check.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Read the log of moves.
steps.prompt:
You are the runtime of a state graph. Run the ticket below. Print one line per transition in this format:
NODE -> NEXT_NODE | reason | state

Nodes: classify, lookup_order, check_refund, human_approval, send_reply, END
Edges:
- classify -> lookup_order if the ticket is about an order
- classify -> send_reply otherwise
- lookup_order -> check_refund if the customer asks for money back
- lookup_order -> send_reply otherwise
- check_refund -> human_approval if the refund is more than 5000 BDT
- check_refund -> send_reply if the refund is 5000 BDT or less
- human_approval -> send_reply (after approval)
- send_reply -> END
You may use only these edges. If a node has no data, invent short fake data and mark it as FAKE.

Ticket #8841: "My laptop bag order #5521 arrived torn. I paid 7500 BDT. I want my money back."
steps.expect: About 5 lines, each with NODE -> NEXT_NODE | reason | state. The log ends with send_reply -> END.
steps.example:
classify -> lookup_order | ticket is about order #5521 | state: category=order
lookup_order -> check_refund | customer wants money back | state: order #5521, paid 7500 BDT (FAKE)
check_refund -> human_approval | 7500 BDT is more than 5000 BDT | state: refund=7500 BDT
human_approval -> send_reply | approved (FAKE) | state: approved=true
send_reply -> END | reply sent | state: done

steps.do: Find the line that starts with check_refund. Check that it goes to human_approval, because 7500 is more than 5000.
steps.expect: Yes: the refund goes to human_approval before send_reply. If a line breaks an edge rule, mark it.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Read how the model describes its work.
steps.prompt:
You are a support agent. Handle this ticket in any way you think best. Then describe, step by step, what you did.

Ticket #8841: "My laptop bag order #5521 arrived torn. I paid 7500 BDT. I want my money back."
Refunds over 5000 BDT need a human to approve them.
steps.expect: A story in words, for example that the model checked the order and asked a human to approve. There is no log of named steps.
steps.example: I read the ticket and saw that the customer wants a refund for a torn bag. I checked order #5521. The refund is 7500 BDT, which is over 5000 BDT, so I asked a human to approve it. After approval I sent the customer a reply and the refund details.

steps.do: Look at both answers. Which one lets you point to one exact line where the approval happened? Write down chat 1 or chat 2.
steps.expect: Chat 1. It has a line named human_approval. Chat 2 only gives a story that you must trust.

en.learned: In chat 1 the model followed a graph: named steps joined by rules. Each move is one line in the log, so you can check it against the rules. In chat 2 you got only a story after the fact. For money, a log that you can check is safer than a story that you must trust.
en.done: You have a log that goes from classify to END, and you checked that the 7500 BDT refund went to human_approval.

check.question: Why is a graph easier to check than a free-form loop?
check.answer: Every step has a name, every move has a rule, and every move is written in the log. So you can see the path and compare it with the rules.

en.challenge: Add one new rule to the first prompt: check_refund -> send_reply if the order is older than 30 days. Send a ticket with an old order. Does the log follow the new rule?

bn.title: একটা support ticket graph দিয়ে চালাও

steps.prompt:
তুমি একটা state graph-এর runtime। নিচের ticket-টা চালাও। প্রতিটা transition-এর জন্য একটা করে লাইন লেখো, এই format-এ:
NODE -> NEXT_NODE | কারণ | state

Node: classify, lookup_order, check_refund, human_approval, send_reply, END
Edge:
- classify -> lookup_order, যদি ticket কোনো order নিয়ে হয়
- classify -> send_reply, না হলে
- lookup_order -> check_refund, যদি customer টাকা ফেরত চায়
- lookup_order -> send_reply, না হলে
- check_refund -> human_approval, যদি refund 5000 BDT-র বেশি হয়
- check_refund -> send_reply, যদি refund 5000 BDT বা তার কম হয়
- human_approval -> send_reply (approval-এর পর)
- send_reply -> END
শুধু এই edge-গুলোই ব্যবহার করতে পারবে। কোনো node-এর data না থাকলে ছোট নকল data বানাও এবং তার পাশে FAKE লেখো।

Ticket #8841: "আমার laptop bag-এর order #5521 ছেঁড়া অবস্থায় এসেছে। আমি 7500 BDT দিয়েছি। আমি টাকা ফেরত চাই।"
steps.expect: প্রায় ৫টা লাইন, প্রতিটা NODE -> NEXT_NODE | কারণ | state format-এ। log শেষ হয় send_reply -> END দিয়ে।
steps.example:
classify -> lookup_order | ticket টা order #5521 নিয়ে | state: category=order
lookup_order -> check_refund | customer টাকা ফেরত চায় | state: order #5521, paid 7500 BDT (FAKE)
check_refund -> human_approval | 7500 BDT, যা 5000 BDT-র বেশি | state: refund=7500 BDT
human_approval -> send_reply | approved (FAKE) | state: approved=true
send_reply -> END | reply পাঠানো হয়েছে | state: done

steps.expect: হ্যাঁ: refund send_reply-এর আগে human_approval-এ যায়। কোনো লাইন edge-এর নিয়ম ভাঙলে সেটা চিহ্ন দিয়ে রাখো।

steps.do: এই prompt টা copy করো, paste করে Enter চাপো। model তার কাজ কীভাবে বলে, তা পড়ো।
steps.prompt:
তুমি একজন support agent। এই ticket-টা তোমার সবচেয়ে ভালো মনে হওয়া যেকোনো উপায়ে সামলাও। তারপর ধাপে ধাপে বলো তুমি কী করেছ।

Ticket #8841: "আমার laptop bag-এর order #5521 ছেঁড়া অবস্থায় এসেছে। আমি 7500 BDT দিয়েছি। আমি টাকা ফেরত চাই।"
5000 BDT-র বেশি refund-এ একজন মানুষকে approve করতে হয়।

bn.done: তোমার কাছে classify থেকে END পর্যন্ত একটা log আছে, আর তুমি দেখেছ 7500 BDT-র refund-টা human_approval-এ গেছে।

sections.title: Agent memory: scratchpad, semantic, procedural
sections.sub: Three memory types show up again and again in the agent literature.[8]

bn.title: Agent-এর memory: scratchpad, semantic, procedural
bn.sub: Agent নিয়ে লেখা গবেষণায় বারবার তিন ধরনের memory আসে।[8]

body.html: The scratchpad is the model's private notes for the current run. When the run ends, the scratchpad is discarded.

Semantic memory stores facts the agent has learned about the user, the project, the world. The classic implementation is a vector store indexed by meaning, plus a structured row store for exact matches.
Procedural memory is the agent's playbook: "how to do X." Stored as versioned prompt templates or Markdown checklists.

items: Too much memory: the agent over-relies on stale facts.
Too little memory: the agent re-derives the same conclusion on every turn.
Conflicting memory: two facts disagree.

layman.html: Agents have three kinds of memory, just like humans.

• Scratchpad = the napkin you're scribbling on right now.
• Semantic memory = facts you remember.
• Procedural memory = how-tos.
The hard part of memory is decay. Stale facts cause confidently wrong answers.
When memory breaks: too much = clings to old facts. Too little = re-derives. Conflicting = flip-flops.

blocks.html: The-colleague analogy: a new hire's scratchpad is the sticky note. Their semantic memory is the facts you told them. Their procedural memory is the standard operating procedures. A good manager keeps all three fresh.

bangla.html: তিন ধরনের মেমরি: Scratchpad (working memory), Semantic memory (long-term facts), Procedural memory (skills)।
মেমরি যেখানে ভাঙে: খুব বেশি = পুরোনো তথ্যে আঁকড়ে থাকে। খুব কম = পুনঃউদ্ভাবন। বিরোধী = দোল খায়।

blocks.html: সহকর্মীর উপমা: নতুন কর্মীর scratchpad হলো sticky note। তাদের semantic memory হলো আপনি যে তথ্য বলেছেন। তাদের procedural memory হলো standard operating procedures।

en.title: Sort facts into three kinds of memory
en.why: When you build a personal assistant, it must keep some facts for months and forget others at once. It must also not trust an old fact when a newer one exists.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Read the three memory lists at the end.
steps.prompt:
You are a personal assistant agent with three memory stores:
- SCRATCHPAD: notes for this run only. It is deleted when the run ends.
- SEMANTIC: lasting facts about the user and the world.
- PROCEDURAL: how-to playbooks for tasks.

Conversation:
User: "Hi, I am Rahim. I am vegetarian and I live in Chattogram. Plan a dinner for 6 people on Friday. Budget 3000 BDT. Whenever I ask for a dinner plan, always give me a shopping list first, then a cooking order."

Do the task briefly. Then print the memory after the run in three sections: SCRATCHPAD, SEMANTIC, PROCEDURAL. After each item, write one short reason why it belongs there. Say which items you will delete.
steps.expect: A short dinner plan, then three lists named SCRATCHPAD, SEMANTIC and PROCEDURAL, each item with a short reason.
steps.example:
SCRATCHPAD:
- Draft menu and cost sums (only needed for this plan)
- Budget 3000 BDT for Friday (one-time)
SEMANTIC:
- Rahim is vegetarian (lasting fact)
- Rahim lives in Chattogram (lasting fact)
PROCEDURAL:
- For a dinner plan: shopping list first, then cooking order (a how-to rule)
I will delete the SCRATCHPAD items when the run ends.

steps.do: Read the lists. Write down which list holds each of these: the draft menu, vegetarian, and the shopping list first rule.
steps.expect: Draft menu in SCRATCHPAD, vegetarian in SEMANTIC, and shopping list first in PROCEDURAL. Models may put the budget in a different list.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. See what the model does with two facts that disagree.
steps.prompt:
You are an assistant with this memory:
SEMANTIC:
- [saved 2023-02-10] User lives in Dhaka.
- [saved 2024-09-05] User lives in Chattogram.
- [saved 2024-01-20] User is vegetarian.

User: "Which city should I look at for a weekend flower market near me?"

Answer the question. Then tell me which memory items you used, and if any items conflict, what you will do about it.
steps.expect: A good answer names Chattogram, sees that Dhaka and Chattogram conflict, and prefers the newer date. It does not need to know real flower markets.
steps.example:
Look at Chattogram for a weekend flower market.
Memory used: "User lives in Chattogram" (saved 2024-09-05).
Conflict: another item says the user lives in Dhaka (saved 2023-02-10). The Chattogram fact is newer, so I trust it and treat the Dhaka fact as old. I would replace it in memory.

en.learned: An agent can keep 3 kinds of memory. Scratchpad holds notes for one run only. Semantic memory holds lasting facts, such as the city of the user. Procedural memory holds how-to rules, such as shopping list first. When two facts disagree, the agent needs a rule, for example the newer date wins.
en.done: You have seen the model sort items into 3 lists, and you have seen it choose Chattogram over Dhaka.

check.question: Why is an old saved fact risky for an agent?
check.answer: Facts can change. If the agent trusts the old fact, it acts on wrong data. It needs dates and a rule to prefer the newer fact.

en.challenge: Add a fourth line to the memory in the last prompt: [saved 2025-03-01] User moved to Sylhet. Does the model now answer Sylhet, and does it say how sure it is?

bn.title: তিন ধরনের memory-তে তথ্য সাজাও
bn.why: তুমি যখন একটা personal assistant বানাবে, তখন তাকে কিছু তথ্য মাসের পর মাস মনে রাখতে হবে, আর কিছু তথ্য সঙ্গে সঙ্গে ভুলে যেতে হবে। নতুন তথ্য থাকলে পুরোনো তথ্যকে বিশ্বাস করাও চলবে না।

steps.do: এই prompt টা copy করো, paste করে Enter চাপো। শেষের তিনটা memory-র তালিকা পড়ো।
steps.prompt:
তুমি একটা personal assistant agent। তোমার তিনটা memory store আছে:
- SCRATCHPAD: শুধু এই run-এর জন্য note। run শেষ হলে এটা মুছে যায়।
- SEMANTIC: ব্যবহারকারী আর দুনিয়া নিয়ে স্থায়ী তথ্য।
- PROCEDURAL: কাজের how-to নিয়ম।

কথোপকথন:
User: "হাই, আমি রহিম। আমি নিরামিষভোজী আর আমি Chattogram-এ থাকি। শুক্রবার ৬ জনের জন্য একটা রাতের খাবারের plan করে দাও। বাজেট 3000 BDT। আমি যখনই রাতের খাবারের plan চাইব, আগে একটা বাজারের তালিকা দেবে, তারপর রান্নার ক্রম।"

কাজটা সংক্ষেপে করো। তারপর run-এর পরের memory তিনটা অংশে লেখো: SCRATCHPAD, SEMANTIC, PROCEDURAL। প্রতিটা item-এর পরে একটা ছোট কারণ লেখো, কেন সেটা ওখানে। কোন item-গুলো মুছে ফেলবে, তা বলো।
steps.expect: রাতের খাবারের একটা ছোট plan, তারপর SCRATCHPAD, SEMANTIC আর PROCEDURAL নামের তিনটা তালিকা, প্রতিটা item-এর পাশে ছোট কারণ।
steps.example:
SCRATCHPAD:
- খসড়া menu আর খরচের হিসাব (শুধু এই plan-এর জন্য লাগে)
- শুক্রবারের বাজেট 3000 BDT (একবারের জন্য)
SEMANTIC:
- রহিম নিরামিষভোজী (স্থায়ী তথ্য)
- রহিম Chattogram-এ থাকে (স্থায়ী তথ্য)
PROCEDURAL:
- রাতের খাবারের plan-এ আগে বাজারের তালিকা, তারপর রান্নার ক্রম (how-to নিয়ম)
run শেষ হলে আমি SCRATCHPAD-এর item-গুলো মুছে ফেলব।

steps.do: তালিকাগুলো পড়ো। এই তিনটা কোন তালিকায় আছে, লিখে রাখো: খসড়া menu, নিরামিষভোজী, আর আগে বাজারের তালিকা নিয়মটা।
steps.expect: খসড়া menu SCRATCHPAD-এ, নিরামিষভোজী SEMANTIC-এ, আর আগে বাজারের তালিকা PROCEDURAL-এ। বাজেট model ভেদে অন্য তালিকায় যেতে পারে।

steps.do: এই prompt টা copy করো, paste করে Enter চাপো। দুটো তথ্য না মিললে model কী করে, তা দেখো।
steps.prompt:
তুমি একজন assistant। তোমার memory এমন:
SEMANTIC:
- [saved 2023-02-10] User Dhaka-য় থাকে।
- [saved 2024-09-05] User Chattogram-এ থাকে।
- [saved 2024-01-20] User নিরামিষভোজী।

User: "আমার কাছাকাছি সপ্তাহান্তের একটা ফুলের বাজারের জন্য আমি কোন শহরটা দেখব?"

প্রশ্নের উত্তর দাও। তারপর বলো তুমি memory-র কোন item-গুলো ব্যবহার করেছ, আর কোনো item-এর মধ্যে গরমিল থাকলে তুমি তা নিয়ে কী করবে।
steps.expect: ভালো উত্তরে Chattogram-এর নাম থাকে, Dhaka আর Chattogram-এর গরমিলটা ধরা পড়ে, আর নতুন তারিখের তথ্যকে প্রাধান্য দেওয়া হয়। model-কে সত্যিকারের ফুলের বাজার জানতে হবে না।
steps.example:
সপ্তাহান্তের ফুলের বাজারের জন্য Chattogram দেখো।
ব্যবহৃত memory: "User Chattogram-এ থাকে" (saved 2024-09-05)।
গরমিল: আরেকটা item বলছে User Dhaka-য় থাকে (saved 2023-02-10)। Chattogram-এর তথ্যটা নতুন, তাই আমি সেটাকে বিশ্বাস করছি আর Dhaka-র তথ্যকে পুরোনো ধরছি। আমি memory-তে সেটা বদলে দেব।

bn.learned: একটা agent ৩ ধরনের memory রাখতে পারে। Scratchpad শুধু একটা run-এর note রাখে। Semantic memory স্থায়ী তথ্য রাখে, যেমন user-এর শহর। Procedural memory how-to নিয়ম রাখে, যেমন আগে বাজারের তালিকা। দুটো তথ্য না মিললে agent-এর একটা নিয়ম লাগে, যেমন নতুন তারিখেরটাই জেতে।
bn.done: তুমি দেখেছ model ৩টা তালিকায় item সাজিয়েছে, আর দেখেছ সে Dhaka-র বদলে Chattogram বেছেছে।

check.question: agent-এর জন্য পুরোনো সংরক্ষিত তথ্য ঝুঁকির কেন?
check.answer: তথ্য বদলে যেতে পারে। agent পুরোনো তথ্য বিশ্বাস করলে ভুল data নিয়ে কাজ করে। তার তারিখ আর নতুন তথ্যকে বেছে নেওয়ার একটা নিয়ম দরকার।

sections.title: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints
sections.sub: Most production agents need at least one approval step.

bn.title: Human-in-the-loop checkpoint (মানুষের অনুমোদনের ধাপ)
bn.sub: বেশিরভাগ production agent-এ অন্তত একটা approval ধাপ লাগে।

items: Read-only: search, fetch, query. Auto-approve.
Local-write: edit a file the agent owns. Auto-approve with a soft cap.
External-write: send an email, post to Slack. Approve per call.
Money: refund, charge, payout. Approve per call, plus a daily cap.
Destructive: delete a record. Two-person rule.

body.html: Every durable framework exposes a "wait for human" primitive. In LangGraph it's interrupt; in Temporal it's wait_for_signal; in Restate it's await call().ack().

# LangGraph interrupt + resume
def send_email(state):
    approval = interrupt({
        "to": state["recipient"],
        "subject": state["subject"],
        "body": state["draft"],
    })
    if not approval["approved"]:
        return {"messages": ["User rejected email send."]}
    email_client.send(approval)
    return {"messages": ["Email sent."]}

blocks.html: The hard part is the UI, not the protocol. Most teams underestimate how much work the approval surface is. The framework gives you a clean "interrupt" primitive, but you still have to build the inbox, the diff view, the approve/reject buttons, the audit log, the SLA, the mobile notifications. Budget at least 30% of agent project time for the human-facing surface.

body.html: When the human can't respond synchronously:

items: Soft timeout + default reject: if no response in 24 hours, the workflow terminates.
Soft timeout + default approve with rollback: if no response, the action proceeds but is logged and reversible.
Hard timeout + escalate: at 24 hours, route to a backup approver.

layman.html: Some actions are too dangerous to do without asking.
The "risk ladder": as actions get more dangerous, more humans need to be in the loop.
The hard part is the UI, not the protocol.
When the human is offline: cancel after 24h, proceed anyway but log it, or escalate to a backup approver.

blocks.html: The new-intern analogy: a new intern can answer the phone without asking. They can take a message. They can draft an email — but show it to you before sending. They can refund a customer under $50 — but you pre-approve the policy. They can fire a customer — only with you in the room.

bangla.html: "Risk ladder": কর্ম যত বিপজ্জনক হয়, তত বেশি মানুষ loop-এ থাকতে হবে।
কঠিন অংশ UI, protocol নয়।
যখন মানুষ offline: 24 ঘণ্টা পর কর্ম বাতিল, যাই হোক এগিয়ে যান কিন্তু লগ করুন, বা backup approver-এ escalate করুন।

blocks.html: নতুন ইন্টার্নের উপমা: নতুন ইন্টার্ন জিজ্ঞাসা ছাড়াই ফোন ধরতে পারে। তারা ইমেল draft করতে পারে — কিন্তু পাঠানোর আগে আপনাকে দেখায়।

en.title: Make an agent wait for your approval
en.why: When an AI agent can refund money or delete data, one wrong step can cost real money. A checkpoint makes the agent stop and ask a human first.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Note which action the agent runs alone and where it stops.
steps.prompt:
You are a support agent with a risk ladder:
- Read-only (search, look up): do it without asking.
- External-write (send an email, post a message): ask me before each call.
- Money (refund, charge): ask me before each call.
- Destructive (delete a record): ask for approval from TWO people.

When you need approval, print exactly:
APPROVAL REQUEST: <action> | <why> | <risk level>
Then stop and wait. Do not do the action until I reply APPROVED. If I reply REJECTED, change your plan.

Task: Customer Nila Rahman (order #7710) was charged twice for 1800 BDT. Do these things: 1) look up the order, 2) refund 1800 BDT, 3) email her a confirmation, 4) delete the duplicate order record. Start now. Use fake results for any lookup.
steps.expect: The agent does the lookup alone (with a fake result). Then it prints one APPROVAL REQUEST for the refund, with risk level Money, and waits.
steps.example:
Lookup of order #7710 (FAKE result): Nila Rahman was charged twice, 1800 BDT each time.
APPROVAL REQUEST: Refund 1800 BDT to Nila Rahman for order #7710 | she was charged twice | Money
I am waiting for your reply.

steps.do: Say no. Copy this reply, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: REJECTED: The customer asked for store credit, not a refund to her card. Change your plan.
steps.expect: The agent changes the plan and sends a new request, for example store credit. It does not repeat the same refund request.
steps.example:
Understood. I will give store credit instead of a card refund.
APPROVAL REQUEST: Give Nila Rahman 1800 BDT store credit | she asked for credit, not a card refund | Money

steps.do: Say yes. Type APPROVED and press Enter.
steps.expect: The agent does the store credit, then asks to send the email. Most chats show the risk level External-write.
steps.example:
Store credit of 1800 BDT given (FAKE result).
APPROVAL REQUEST: Email Nila Rahman a confirmation of the store credit | tell her the problem is fixed | External-write

steps.do: Say yes again. Type APPROVED and press Enter.
steps.expect: The agent sends the email, then asks to delete the duplicate record. This time it asks for approval from two people.
steps.example:
Email sent (FAKE).
APPROVAL REQUEST: Delete the duplicate order record for #7710 | the customer was charged twice | Destructive
This needs approval from TWO people. Please reply APPROVED from two different people.

en.learned: The agent has a risk ladder: it runs safe actions alone and stops for risky ones. It prints a request and waits, so a human decides. When you rejected the refund, the agent changed its plan and did not repeat itself. For the most risky action, delete, it asked for two people.
en.done: You have seen the agent run the lookup alone, stop at each risky action, and ask for two approvals for the delete.

check.question: Why does the agent run the lookup alone but stop before the refund?
check.answer: A lookup only reads data and cannot cause harm. A refund moves money and is hard to undo, so a human must approve it first.

en.challenge: Add this rule to the first prompt: If I do not reply for 24 hours, the default is REJECT. Ask the agent what it does next. Then ask what changes if the default is APPROVE.

bn.title: agent-কে তোমার approval-এর জন্য অপেক্ষা করাও
bn.why: একটা AI agent যখন টাকা refund করতে বা data মুছতে পারে, তখন একটা ভুল ধাপে সত্যিকারের টাকা যেতে পারে। checkpoint agent-কে থামায়, যাতে সে আগে একজন মানুষকে জিজ্ঞেস করে।

sections.title: Subagents and delegation patterns
sections.sub: When a single agent's task list grows too large for one context window, the natural move is to delegate.

bn.title: Subagent আর delegation pattern
bn.sub: একটা agent-এর কাজের তালিকা যখন এক context window-এর জন্য বেশি বড় হয়ে যায়, তখন স্বাভাবিক সমাধান হলো কাজ ভাগ করে অন্যকে দেওয়া (delegate)।

body.html: A subagent is an agent launched by another agent. It has its own system prompt, its own tool surface, its own loop, and its own termination. It returns a final result to the parent — not intermediate state.

The mental model is "manager → worker," not "fork/join." The parent does not poll the subagent. The parent does not stream the subagent's progress. The parent waits for the subagent to finish, then receives a single, structured result. The benefit: the parent's context window stays clean.

Anthropic's Claude Code ships a Task tool that the model can invoke to spawn a subagent. The subagent runs in its own loop, with its own tools, and returns a summary. The parent never sees the intermediate steps — only the summary. This is the cleanest implementation of the pattern in 2025.

OpenAI's openai-agents-sdk exposes Runner.run(agent, input) returning a final RunResult. CrewAI models multi-agent systems as crews (the team), agents (the roles), tasks (the work), and a process (sequential, hierarchical, or consensual).

items: The subtask is well-defined and self-contained.
The subtask needs different tools than the parent has.
The subtask's intermediate steps would pollute the parent's context.
You want the subtask to be retried independently of the parent.
You want to bill the subtask to a different cost centre.

layman.html: A subagent is a temporary worker you hire to do one job. You give them a brief, a list of tools they can use, and a deadline. They go do the work and come back with an answer. You never see what they did in the middle — just the final report.
Mental model: the parent is the manager. The subagent is a contractor.
Bonus: you can use a different (cheaper) model for the subagent.

blocks.html: The contractor analogy: a CEO doesn't personally do market research. They hire a research firm, give them a brief, get a report.

bangla.html: Subagent হলো একটি অস্থায়ী কর্মী যাকে আপনি একটি কাজ করতে নিয়োগ করেন।
Manager-worker, fork/join নয়।
কখন subagent ব্যবহার করবেন: উপ-কাজ সু-সংজ্ঞায়িত, ভিন্ন tools দরকার, parent-এর context দূষিত করবে, স্বাধীনভাবে retry করতে চান।

blocks.html: ঠিকাদারের উপমা: একজন CEO ব্যক্তিগতভাবে market research করেন না। তারা একটি research firm নিয়োগ করেন।

en.title: Write a brief that a subagent can use
en.why: When you build a big agent, it can hand a small job to a helper agent. The helper starts with an empty head, so a weak brief gives a wrong or useless result.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Then select the whole brief that the model writes and copy it.
steps.prompt:
You are a manager agent. Your context is long, and you want to delegate one task to a subagent. The subagent will NOT see this conversation.

Your context so far:
- The user is a freelance designer, Tania Akter, who got a contract from the company BlueLeaf Ltd.
- Payment terms: 60 days after invoice. Tania wants 30 days or less.
- Clause 9 says: "Either side may end this contract with 7 days written notice." Tania wants at least 30 days.
- Clause 12 says BlueLeaf owns all work, even drafts that were not paid for.
- The user wants a short list of risks, not legal advice.

Delegate: review clauses 9 and 12. Write the brief for the subagent. It must include: goal, all the facts the subagent needs, what to avoid, and the output format (maximum 5 lines). Print only the brief.
steps.expect: A brief with 4 parts: goal, facts (both clauses, the user, the company), what to avoid, and the output format.
steps.example:
GOAL: Review clauses 9 and 12 of a contract and list the risks for the freelancer.
FACTS: The freelancer is Tania Akter. The company is BlueLeaf Ltd. Clause 9: "Either side may end this contract with 7 days written notice." Tania wants at least 30 days. Clause 12: BlueLeaf owns all work, even drafts that were not paid for.
AVOID: Do not give legal advice. Do not review other clauses.
OUTPUT: A list of risks, maximum 5 lines.

steps.do: You are the subagent now. Paste the brief you copied in step 1 as your message and press Enter.
steps.expect: A short list of risks, 5 lines at most, about clause 9 (7 days notice) and clause 12 (BlueLeaf owns unpaid drafts).
steps.example:
- Clause 9: either side can end the contract with only 7 days notice. Tania wants at least 30 days. Risk: she can lose the job fast.
- Clause 12: BlueLeaf owns all work, even drafts that were not paid for. Risk: she can lose work without payment.
- Both points are worth raising with BlueLeaf before Tania signs.

steps.do: Now try a weak brief. Copy this message, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Review the clauses we talked about earlier and tell me if they are a problem for the user. Use the same format as before.
steps.expect: The model has no idea what you mean. It asks which clauses you mean, or it invents details.
steps.example: I cannot see an earlier conversation. Which clauses do you mean, and who is the user? Please send the text of the clauses and the format you want.

steps.do: Copy this question, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: What information was missing from my message?
steps.expect: A list such as: the text of the clauses, who the user is, what to look for, and the output format.
steps.example:
- The text of the clauses
- Who the user is and what the user wants
- What to look for
- The output format you wanted

en.learned: A subagent starts with an empty context: it cannot see your earlier chat. So the brief must hold the goal, the facts, what to avoid, and the output format. In chat 2 the brief did that, and the result was clear. In chat 3 it did not, so the model had to ask or guess.
en.done: You have a short list of risks from chat 2, and a list of missing information from chat 3.

check.question: Why must a manager agent write a brief that holds everything?
check.answer: A subagent starts with its own empty context and sees nothing of the manager's chat. It can only work with what the brief says. The manager then gets back one short result.

bn.title: subagent-এর জন্য একটা কাজের brief লেখো
bn.why: তুমি যখন একটা বড় agent বানাবে, সে একটা ছোট কাজ সাহায্যকারী agent-কে দিতে পারে। সাহায্যকারী agent শুরু করে একদম খালি মাথায়, তাই দুর্বল brief হলে উত্তর ভুল বা কাজে না-লাগার মতো হয়।

steps.prompt:
তুমি একজন manager agent। তোমার context অনেক লম্বা, আর তুমি একটা কাজ একটা subagent-কে দিতে চাও। subagent এই কথোপকথন দেখতে পাবে না।

তোমার এ পর্যন্ত context:
- user একজন freelance designer, তানিয়া আক্তার। সে BlueLeaf Ltd কোম্পানির কাছ থেকে একটা contract পেয়েছে।
- payment-এর শর্ত: invoice-এর 60 দিন পরে। তানিয়া চায় 30 দিন বা তার কম।
- Clause 9 বলে: "যেকোনো পক্ষ 7 দিনের লিখিত notice দিয়ে এই contract শেষ করতে পারবে।" তানিয়া চায় অন্তত 30 দিন।
- Clause 12 বলে, যে কাজের টাকা দেওয়া হয়নি সেই খসড়াসহ সব কাজের মালিক BlueLeaf।
- user চায় ঝুঁকির একটা ছোট তালিকা, আইনি পরামর্শ নয়।

কাজ দাও: clause 9 আর 12 দেখো। subagent-এর জন্য brief লেখো। তাতে থাকতে হবে: লক্ষ্য, subagent-এর যত তথ্য লাগবে, কী এড়াতে হবে, আর উত্তরের format (সর্বোচ্চ ৫ লাইন)। শুধু brief-টা লেখো।
steps.expect: ৪ অংশের একটা brief: লক্ষ্য, তথ্য (দুটো clause, user, কোম্পানি), কী এড়াতে হবে, আর উত্তরের format।

তথ্য: freelancer-এর নাম তানিয়া আক্তার। কোম্পানি BlueLeaf Ltd। Clause 9: "যেকোনো পক্ষ 7 দিনের লিখিত notice দিয়ে এই contract শেষ করতে পারবে।" তানিয়া চায় অন্তত 30 দিন। Clause 12: যে কাজের টাকা দেওয়া হয়নি সেই খসড়াসহ সব কাজের মালিক BlueLeaf।
এড়াও: আইনি পরামর্শ দেবে না। অন্য clause দেখবে না।
উত্তরের format: ঝুঁকির তালিকা, সর্বোচ্চ ৫ লাইন।

sections.title: Error recovery, retries, and self-correction
sections.sub: Three escalating layers: retry the same call, fall back to a different one, or reflect on the failure and revise. Always bound retries.

bn.title: Error recovery, retry আর self-correction
bn.sub: তিন ধাপের উপায়, ধাপে ধাপে বড় হয়: একই call আবার করা, অন্য একটা উপায়ে যাওয়া (fallback), অথবা ব্যর্থতাটা নিয়ে ভেবে (reflect) ঠিক করে নেওয়া। Retry-র একটা সীমা সবসময় বেঁধে দিন।

body.html: Transient failures (rate limit, network blip, server overloaded) are best handled with a short retry. Exponential backoff is the default: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, with jitter to avoid thundering-herd. Cap at 3–5 attempts; beyond that, the failure is not transient.

# Exponential backoff with jitter
import random, time
def retry_with_backoff(fn, max_attempts=5, base=1.0):
    for attempt in range(max_attempts):
        try:
            return fn()
        except (RateLimitError, TimeoutError):
            if attempt == max_attempts - 1: raise
            sleep = base * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, base)
            time.sleep(sleep)

When the failure is not transient (the API is permanently down, the JSON schema is rejected because the model can't follow it, the function raised a domain-specific error), retrying the same call is pointless. Fall back to a different tool or model: use a smaller model with a simpler schema, use a different vendor, or skip the tool and let the model answer from its own knowledge.

When the failure was caused by a reasoning error (the model called the right tool with the wrong arguments, or made a logical mistake), neither retry nor fallback fixes the root cause. Feed the failure back into the model and ask it to revise.[3] Reflexion is the formal version of this.

blocks.html: Unbounded retry is a footgun. A poisoned input that always returns the same transient-looking error will burn your entire budget in a tight retry loop. Always set a hard cap on retries, a wall-clock timeout, and a circuit breaker that opens after N consecutive failures of the same type.

body.html: A circuit breaker protects against a downstream service that's failing in a way that looks transient but isn't. After 5 consecutive failures of the same kind, the breaker opens: all calls for the next 60 seconds fail fast with a "service unavailable" error, no retries. After 60 seconds, the breaker half-opens: one test call. If it succeeds, the breaker closes. If it fails, the timer resets.

layman.html: Three layers of failure handling:

• Retry: try the same thing again.
• Fallback: try a different thing.
• Reflect: feed the error back to the AI.
The dangerous footgun: an unbounded retry will burn your entire budget. Always cap retries.
The circuit breaker pattern: after 5 consecutive failures, all calls for the next 60 seconds fail instantly.

blocks.html: The-customer-service analogy: when a customer's call drops, you call them back. If it drops a third time, you send an email instead.

bangla.html: ব্যর্থতা মোকাবেলার তিনটি স্তর: Retry, Fallback, Reflect।
বিপজ্জনক footgun: একই ত্রুটি বারবার আসতে থাকলে, একটি unbounded retry একটি টাইট loop-এ আপনার সম্পূর্ণ budget পুড়িয়ে ফেলবে।
Circuit breaker pattern: 5 টি ধারাবাহিক ব্যর্থতার পর, পরবর্তী 60 সেকেন্ডের জন্য সমস্ত call তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে ব্যর্থ হয়।

blocks.html: কাস্টমার সার্ভিসের উপমা: যখন একজন গ্রাহকের কল ড্রপ হয়, আপনি তাদের কল করেন। এটি তৃতীয়বার ড্রপ হলে, আপনি পরিবর্তে একটি ইমেল পাঠান।

en.title: See an agent retry, fix, and fall back
en.why: When your agent calls a weather or payment service, some calls fail. It must retry short failures, fix its own mistakes, and give up in time, or it wastes money.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt:
You are an agent with one tool: get_weather(city). I play the tool and send you the result.

Error rules:
1. Temporary error (rate limit, timeout): wait and retry the same call. Allow at most 3 retries.
2. Permanent error (service down, no ETA): do not keep retrying. Fall back: answer from your own knowledge and say clearly that it is NOT verified.
3. Wrong-argument error: read the message, fix the argument, and call again.

Reply each turn with either:
ACTION: get_weather("...")
or
FINAL: your answer

Goal: Tell me today's weather in Dacca.
steps.expect: One line only, for example ACTION: get_weather("Dacca").
steps.example: ACTION: get_weather("Dacca")

steps.do: Now you are the tool. Copy this error, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: ERROR 400: unknown city "Dacca". Did you mean "Dhaka"?
steps.expect: The agent fixes the spelling and calls again, for example ACTION: get_weather("Dhaka").
steps.example: ACTION: get_weather("Dhaka")

steps.do: Send a second error. Copy this text, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: ERROR 503: weather service unavailable. No ETA.
steps.expect: Most chats do one of two things: they call the same tool again, or they stop with a FINAL answer marked NOT verified.
steps.example: ACTION: get_weather("Dhaka")

steps.do: If the agent calls again, send the same 503 error again. Repeat until you see a FINAL line. Write down how many times you sent it.
steps.prompt: ERROR 503: weather service unavailable. No ETA.
steps.expect: After no more than 3 retries, the agent writes a FINAL line that says the answer is NOT verified.
steps.example: FINAL: I could not reach the weather service, so this answer is NOT verified. Dhaka is usually warm and humid, and rain is common in many months. Please check a weather site for today.

en.learned: The agent met 3 kinds of error. For the wrong city name (400), it read the message, fixed the argument, and called again. For the service that was down (503), it did not retry for ever and gave a fallback answer marked NOT verified. A retry cap (here, at most 3 retries) stops a loop that never ends and burns your budget.
en.done: You have seen the model fix Dacca to Dhaka, and then write a FINAL line marked NOT verified.

sections.title: Long-running agents and durable execution
sections.sub: Agents that take minutes or hours face three problems a normal Python loop can't solve: crashes lose state, rate limits force waits, and human approvals force pauses. Durable execution engines solve all three.

bn.title: দীর্ঘক্ষণ চলা agent আর durable execution
bn.sub: যে agent কয়েক মিনিট বা কয়েক ঘণ্টা চলে, তার তিনটা সমস্যা সাধারণ Python loop সামলাতে পারে না: crash হলে state হারিয়ে যায়, rate limit-এর জন্য অপেক্ষা করতে হয়, আর human approval-এর জন্য থামতে হয়। Durable execution engine এই তিনটারই সমাধান দেয়।

body.html: The naive solution is to checkpoint the agent's state to disk every step. But "the agent's state" is more than the message log: it's the in-flight tool calls, the partial writes to external services, the human approval state, the retry counters. Saving the messages and losing the rest gives you a corrupt resume.

A durable execution engine records every step's intent and result to a durable store (a database, a journal, a queue). On crash, the next process loads the snapshot and resumes from the next un-run step. The engine handles retries, rate limits, and human-in-the-loop pauses natively. The application code is a series of workflow steps; the engine is the runtime that survives crashes.[7]

layman.html: Long agents need a "save and resume" engine.
The fix: durable execution. Treat the agent as a series of steps. After each step, write progress to a database. If the server crashes, the next process loads that log and resumes at the failed step.
When you need it: the agent runs for more than 30 seconds; humans are in the loop and might take days to respond; the agent makes irreversible side effects.
Pick a tool: Temporal or Restate for traditional, multi-day workflows. Inngest for event-driven. AWS Step Functions if you're all-in on AWS.

en.title: Resume a crashed agent from a journal
en.why: When an agent charges a card and then crashes, it must not charge again after the restart. A journal of every step tells it what is already done.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. Read which steps the agent skips and what it checks first.
steps.prompt:
You are an agent that restarts after a crash. Read the durable journal and decide what to do next.

JOURNAL for workflow INV-2041:
1. fetch_invoice | intent logged | result: OK, amount 4500 BDT, customer Karim Hossain
2. validate_invoice | intent logged | result: OK
3. charge_card (request key INV-2041-charge, a unique ID that stops a double charge) | intent logged | result: MISSING (process crashed)
4. send_receipt_email | not started
5. update_ledger | not started

Tell me: which steps you skip, which step you re-run, what you check before you re-run it, and why. Keep the answer under 120 words.
steps.expect: The agent skips steps 1 and 2. It does not just charge again: it first checks if the charge with the request key already happened. Steps 4 and 5 come later.
steps.example:
Skip: steps 1 and 2, because the journal shows OK.
Re-run: step 3, charge_card, because its result is missing.
Check first: look in the payment system for a charge with key INV-2041-charge. If it exists, do not charge again and use its result. If not, charge 4500 BDT once with the same key.
Then do steps 4 and 5. The key stops a double charge.

steps.do: Copy this prompt, paste it, and press Enter. This agent has only a chat log and no journal.
steps.prompt:
You are an agent that restarts after a crash. You only have the last messages of the chat.

MESSAGE LOG for invoice INV-2041:
- User: Process invoice INV-2041 for Karim Hossain, 4500 BDT.
- Agent: Starting. I will validate the invoice, charge the card, send a receipt, and update the ledger.
- Agent: Invoice is valid. Charging the card now.
[process crashed]

Tell me what you do next, step by step. Keep the answer under 120 words.
steps.expect: The model cannot know if the card was charged before the crash. A careless answer just charges again. A careful answer says it must guess or check.
steps.example: I cannot be sure the card was charged before the crash. I will check the payment records first. If I find no charge, I will charge 4500 BDT, then send the receipt to Karim Hossain and update the ledger. If I find a charge, I will skip the charge.

steps.do: Copy this question, paste it, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: What extra data do you need to be safe?
steps.expect: A list of missing data, for example a record of each step with its result, and a unique key for the charge.
steps.example:
- A record of every step and its result
- A unique key for the charge, so a second charge can be ignored
- A way to check the payment system
- A note of which steps are done and which are not

en.learned: The journal saves each step and its result. After the crash the agent knew that steps 1 and 2 were done and that step 3 was unknown. The chat log does not show if the card was charged, so the second agent had to guess. A system that saves every step like this is called durable execution.
en.done: You have two plans: the first skips done steps and checks the charge, and the second has to guess.

check.question: Why is a saved chat log not enough to resume an agent safely?
check.answer: The log shows what was said, not what really happened. It does not show if a tool call finished or if the card was charged. A journal saves the result of every step.

en.challenge: In the first prompt, change step 3 to result: OK, charged 4500 BDT. What does the agent do now? Why is the plan different?

bn.title: journal দেখে crash হওয়া agent-কে আবার চালাও
bn.why: একটা agent যখন card থেকে টাকা কেটে crash করে, তখন restart-এর পর সে আবার টাকা কাটতে পারবে না। প্রতিটা ধাপের একটা journal তাকে বলে দেয় কোন কাজ আগেই হয়ে গেছে।

steps.do: এই prompt টা copy করো, paste করে Enter চাপো। agent কোন ধাপগুলো বাদ দেয় আর আগে কী যাচাই করে, তা পড়ো। (journal-এর নামগুলো English-এ রাখা হয়েছে।)
steps.prompt:
তুমি একটা agent, যে crash-এর পর আবার চালু হয়। durable journal পড়ো এবং ঠিক করো এরপর কী করবে।

workflow INV-2041-এর JOURNAL:
1. fetch_invoice | intent logged | result: OK, amount 4500 BDT, customer Karim Hossain
2. validate_invoice | intent logged | result: OK
3. charge_card (request key INV-2041-charge, একটা unique ID যা দুইবার টাকা কাটা আটকায়) | intent logged | result: MISSING (process crashed)
4. send_receipt_email | not started
5. update_ledger | not started

বলো: কোন ধাপগুলো তুমি বাদ দেবে, কোন ধাপ আবার চালাবে, আবার চালানোর আগে কী যাচাই করবে, আর কেন। উত্তর ১২০ শব্দের মধ্যে রাখো।
steps.expect: agent ধাপ ১ আর ২ বাদ দেয়। সে সরাসরি আবার টাকা কাটে না: আগে দেখে request key-সহ charge আগেই হয়েছে কি না। ধাপ ৪ আর ৫ পরে আসে।
steps.example:
বাদ দেব: ধাপ ১ আর ২, কারণ journal-এ OK আছে।
আবার চালাব: ধাপ ৩, charge_card, কারণ তার result নেই।
আগে যাচাই: payment system-এ INV-2041-charge key দিয়ে কোনো charge আছে কি না দেখব। থাকলে আর টাকা কাটব না, আর সেই result ব্যবহার করব। না থাকলে একই key দিয়ে একবারই 4500 BDT কাটব।
তারপর ধাপ ৪ আর ৫ করব। key দুইবার টাকা কাটা আটকায়।

steps.do: এই prompt টা copy করো, paste করে Enter চাপো। এই agent-এর কাছে শুধু chat log আছে, কোনো journal নেই।
steps.prompt:
তুমি একটা agent, যে crash-এর পর আবার চালু হয়। তোমার কাছে শুধু chat-এর শেষ message-গুলো আছে।

invoice INV-2041-এর MESSAGE LOG:
- User: কারিম হোসেনের জন্য invoice INV-2041 প্রসেস করো, 4500 BDT।
- Agent: শুরু করছি। আমি invoice যাচাই করব, card থেকে টাকা কাটব, রসিদ পাঠাব এবং ledger update করব।
- Agent: Invoice ঠিক আছে। এখন card থেকে টাকা কাটছি।
[process crash করেছে]

বলো তুমি এরপর কী করবে, ধাপে ধাপে। উত্তর ১২০ শব্দের মধ্যে রাখো।
steps.expect: crash-এর আগে card থেকে টাকা কাটা হয়েছিল কি না, model তা জানতে পারে না। অসাবধান উত্তর আবার টাকা কাটে। সাবধান উত্তর বলে যে তাকে আন্দাজ বা যাচাই করতে হবে।
steps.example: crash-এর আগে card থেকে টাকা কাটা হয়েছিল কি না, আমি নিশ্চিত নই। আমি আগে payment record দেখব। কোনো charge না পেলে 4500 BDT কাটব, তারপর কারিম হোসেনকে রসিদ পাঠাব আর ledger update করব। charge পেলে টাকা কাটার ধাপটা বাদ দেব।

steps.do: এই প্রশ্নটা copy করে paste করো, তারপর Enter চাপো।
steps.prompt: নিরাপদ থাকার জন্য তোমার আর কোন data লাগবে?
steps.expect: না-থাকা data-র একটা তালিকা, যেমন প্রতিটা ধাপ আর তার result-এর record, আর charge-এর জন্য একটা unique key।
steps.example:
- প্রতিটা ধাপ আর তার result-এর record
- charge-এর জন্য একটা unique key, যাতে দ্বিতীয় charge উপেক্ষা করা যায়
- payment system যাচাই করার একটা উপায়
- কোন ধাপ হয়েছে আর কোনটা হয়নি, তার note

bn.learned: journal প্রতিটা ধাপ আর তার result সংরক্ষণ করে। crash-এর পর agent জানত ধাপ ১ আর ২ হয়ে গেছে, আর ধাপ ৩ অজানা। chat log দেখায় না card থেকে টাকা কাটা হয়েছে কি না, তাই দ্বিতীয় agent-কে আন্দাজ করতে হয়েছে। এভাবে প্রতিটা ধাপ সংরক্ষণ করা পদ্ধতির নাম durable execution।
bn.done: তোমার কাছে দুটো plan আছে: প্রথমটা হয়ে যাওয়া ধাপ বাদ দেয় আর charge যাচাই করে, দ্বিতীয়টাকে আন্দাজ করতে হয়।

check.question: agent-কে নিরাপদে আবার চালাতে শুধু সংরক্ষিত chat log যথেষ্ট নয় কেন?
check.answer: log দেখায় কী বলা হয়েছিল, সত্যিই কী ঘটেছিল তা নয়। tool call শেষ হয়েছিল কি না, বা card থেকে টাকা কাটা হয়েছিল কি না, তা log-এ নেই। journal প্রতিটা ধাপের result সংরক্ষণ করে।

bn.challenge: প্রথম prompt-এ ধাপ ৩ বদলে লেখো result: OK, charged 4500 BDT। agent এবার কী করে? plan অন্যরকম কেন?

sections.title: Browser and computer-use agents
sections.sub: The newest agent category uses a model that can see a screenshot and act with mouse/keyboard primitives. OpenAI's Operator and Anthropic's "computer use" are the marquee examples. They trade precision for generality.

bn.title: Browser আর computer-use agent
bn.sub: এটা agent-এর সবচেয়ে নতুন ধরন। এখানে model screenshot দেখতে পারে, আর mouse/keyboard-এর মতো মৌলিক কাজ দিয়ে কাজ করে। উদাহরণ হিসেবে সবচেয়ে পরিচিত OpenAI-র Operator আর Anthropic-এর "computer use"। এরা নিখুঁত হওয়ার বদলে সবকিছুতে কাজ করতে পারাকে বেছে নেয়।

body.html: The model receives a screenshot of the desktop (or a specific window) and a list of available actions: mouse_move, left_click, right_click, type, key, screenshot. It picks an action, the runtime executes it, captures a new screenshot, and feeds both back. The loop continues until the model emits a done action.[9]

# Anthropic computer-use minimal loop (pseudocode)
while not done:
    screenshot = capture()
    response = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-sonnet-4-5",
        tools=["computer"],
        messages=[{"role": "user",
                   "content": [screenshot, goal]}],
    )
    for block in response.content:
        if block.type == "tool_use":
            execute(block.input)
    if response.stop_reason in ("end_turn", "max_tokens"):
        break

items: No API exists. The site or app has no programmatic interface; the only way in is the GUI.
The API is hostile. The vendor's API is rate-limited, expensive, or has bad docs; the GUI is faster.
One-off tasks. You need to do this once, not at scale, so the cost-per-task of computer use is acceptable.
Cross-app workflows. The task crosses SaaS boundaries (read from Gmail, post to Slack) and no integration exists.
Cost. Computer-use calls are 5–30× the cost of an API call (vision tokens for every screenshot).
Latency. A click is instant; a screenshot → LLM → action cycle is 1–5 seconds. A 20-step task takes a minute.
Reliability. A shifted button, a popup, a captcha — any of these kills the run.
Security. The agent has unrestricted mouse/keyboard. Pair with a sandboxed VM, a per-task browser profile, and a tight human-in-the-loop on destructive actions.

body.html: Browser agents (ChatGPT's "Browse with Bing," Perplexity, Arc Max) are a constrained subset of computer use: the model can only see and act inside a single browser tab, not the whole desktop. They use the same screenshot → action loop but with a smaller surface area, which is why they're more reliable. If you can frame the task in a browser, prefer a browser agent over a full computer-use agent.

Production computer-use agents use three reliability patterns: (1) the model emits a structured plan up front ("I will click the blue button, then fill the form, then submit"), which makes mid-run debugging easier; (2) each step is checkpointed, so a crash resumes from the last successful step; (3) the agent runs in an isolated VM or browser profile, so a misclick can't reach the host system.

layman.html: Browser agents and computer-use agents are the "wild west" of AI.
Where they win: no API exists for the site; the API is hostile; one-off tasks where speed doesn't matter; cross-app workflows with no integration.
Where they lose: cost (5–30× more than an API call), latency (1–5 seconds per click vs instant), reliability (a shifted button kills the run), security.
Browser agents vs full computer use: browser agents are constrained to a single browser tab. Smaller surface = more reliable.
The reliability pattern: the model emits a plan up front, each step is checkpointed, and the agent runs in an isolated VM.

blocks.html: The-remote-intern analogy: a remote intern who can only see your screen and use a mouse. Slow, but they can do anything you can do.

bangla.html: Browser agent এবং computer-use agent হলো AI-এর "wild west"।
যেখানে জেতে: সাইটের জন্য API নেই; API প্রতিকূল; one-off কাজ; ক্রস-অ্যাপ workflows।
যেখানে হারে: খরচ, latency, নির্ভরযোগ্যতা, নিরাপত্তা।
Browser agent বনাম সম্পূর্ণ computer use: browser agent একটি একক browser tab-এ সীমাবদ্ধ।

blocks.html: দূরবর্তী ইন্টার্নের উপমা: একজন দূরবর্তী ইন্টার্ন যিনি শুধু আপনার screen দেখতে এবং mouse ব্যবহার করতে পারেন।
